strategy.summary: GET /products (src/app.js listProducts) filters the catalogue by a case-insensitive substring `q`, pages with `limit` (default DEFAULT_LIMIT=20, capped at MAX_LIMIT=50) and `offset` (default 0), returns { total, items }, and refuses non-whole limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Tests start the real app in-process on an OS-chosen port, like the existing test/products.test.js, and assert against the fixed 120-product catalogue.
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
The shop's search box UI (not in this repo)
assumptions: The real app runs in-process via createApp() on port 0 (OS-chosen); nothing is faked.
The cap is the exported MAX_LIMIT (50) and the default page size DEFAULT_LIMIT (20); tests import them rather than hard-coding.
The catalogue is the fixed PRODUCTS list from src/catalogue.js (120 products, 'Name N' for N 1-15); search tests assert on known names/counts from it.
Negative numbers and decimals count as 'not a whole number'.
openQuestions: Should an empty `limit=` / `offset=` be treated as absent (default) or refused? The code refuses it with 400; tests don't pin it.
Should `q` be trimmed of surrounding whitespace? The code does not trim; not tested.

risks.description: Search is case-sensitive or matches only prefixes, so shoppers miss products
risks.mitigation: TC1 uses an upper-case q that matches mid-name and prefix names; TC3 checks no-match gives empty.

risks.description: total reports page size instead of all matches, breaking pagination UI
risks.mitigation: TC4/TC5/TC10 assert total independently of page size.

risks.description: Unbounded limit lets clients dump the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC6 requests 1000 and expects MAX_LIMIT items.

risks.description: Malformed paging params produce NaN slices or 500s
risks.mitigation: TC7-TC9 cover non-numeric, decimal, negative and zero values.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` returns only products whose name contains it case-insensitively; without `q` every product is listed.
Results are paged by `limit` and `offset`, the response's `total` is the number of all matches, and limits above the maximum are capped.
A `limit` or `offset` that isn't a whole number, or a `limit` below 1, gets 400.

testCases.title: matches q anywhere in the name regardless of case
preconditions: app listening on an OS-chosen port
testCases.expected: 200, total 30 (15 Teapot + 15 Tea strainer), every item name contains 'tea' case-insensitively, and both 'Teapot 1' and 'Tea strainer 1' are present

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200, total equals PRODUCTS.length (120), items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products in order

testCases.title: returns no items and a total of 0 when nothing matches q
returns the page selected by limit and offset with the total of all matches
pages through search results with total counting every match
testCases.rationale: total must reflect matches, not catalogue or page

testCases.title: caps a large limit at the maximum page size
returns an empty page when offset is past the last match
refuses a limit that isn't a whole number with 400
testCases.expected: 400 with an error field for each

testCases.title: refuses a limit of 0 with 400 and accepts a limit of 1
testCases.expected: limit=0 gets 400; limit=1 gets 200 with exactly one item

testCases.title: refuses an offset that isn't a whole number with 400
testCases.expected: 400 with an error field for each

strategy.environmentNotes: No services or env vars; the app is started in-process on port 0 by the test file. Runs under the existing `npm test` (vitest run).
